clue.text: Writer's shoes sister regularly removed

indicators.note: every other letter of shoes sister is taken away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: An odd domestic note: a writer's footwear, with his sister routinely taking it away.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike out the odd letters of 'shoes sister' and the even ones remain. The definition is 'Writer' with the 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was the German-Swiss novelist of Steppenwolf and Siddhartha.

clue.text: Detest keeping in one European city for winter

indicators.note: keeping in means holding inside, so the other pieces go within the word for detest

parts.note: to detest is to hate
I is the Roman numeral for one
Bern is the Swiss capital

explanation.surface: Someone loathes being stuck in a European city through the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winter' is a verb here: to spend the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hibernate is to pass the cold season dormant, which is what to winter (verb) can mean.

clue.text: Spy has no open cases

indicators.note: the letters are encased within the words has no open, running across them

explanation.surface: An intelligence agent has no unsolved investigations.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in haS NO OPen.
explanation.definitionFit: To snoop is to pry secretly into others' affairs, so a spy (verb) snoops.

clue.text: Stylish base on a font? Not half!

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
the on side in cricket is also called the leg side

indicators.note: not half means only the second half of the word font is kept

parts.note: the latter half of font gives these letters

explanation.surface: A typographer asks whether a font is a stylish basis, with the slang retort 'Not half!' meaning yes indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, behind a right-hander's legs, is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, the same as stylish.

clue.text: Men do cram around the one in charge

indicators.note: around here means messed about, so the letters of men do cram are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers pack tightly about their leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A commander is the officer who leads and has authority over a unit.

clue.text: Tea party's beginning next to the Spanish place of worship

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: beginning picks out just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A tea party is starting beside a Spanish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room set aside for prayer.

clue.text: I ban no book after marvellous David Copperfield?

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces follow the word for marvellous

parts.note: magic as an adjective means wonderful

indicators.note: no says the letter for book is taken out of ban

explanation.surface: A censor bans no book, after Dickens's marvellous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Dickens's novel; the definition is the American illusionist of the same name, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: David Copperfield is a famous stage illusionist, an example of a conjurer.

clue.text: One coming from Nigeria, maybe, in a craft at sea with temperature dropping

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of in a craft are jumbled
dropping says one letter is left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: A traveller from West Africa sails aboard a boat as the weather cools.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from INACRAFT and rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a country on that continent, so its citizens are examples, signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Concludes dish almost cracks

indicators.note: almost means the word dish loses its final letter

parts.note: to crack a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: A finale in which a plate nearly breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' suggests breakage, but it means solves, as in cracking a code.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve a parliament or partnership is to bring it formally to an end.

clue.text: Critical points with no Conservative rebels

indicators.note: with no says the letter for Conservative is removed from the word for critical points

parts.note: crises are turning points or moments of danger

explanation.surface: At key moments, rebels act without Tory support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' is a verb: rises up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise (in revolt) is to rebel against authority, so rises matches the verb rebels.

clue.text: Returning weapon?

parts.note: the whole clue describes the curved Australian throwing stick that comes back to its thrower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' might suggest a reversal of a word for weapon, but the clue is a plain description.
explanation.definitionFit: This curved throwing implement is famous for flying in an arc back to the person who threw it.

clue.text: Flowers put back in greenhouses, originally

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit within the words that follow, across their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Plants are returned to the glasshouses where they first grew.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is what signals the letters lying within greenhouseS ORiginally; 'put back' then reads them in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are among the best-known garden blooms, which is what flowers names here.

clue.text: Salesman with decorative fabric giving change

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
lace is an openwork ornamental fabric

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman carries ornamental cloth and gives his customers small coins back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like a noun (coins) but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to substitute another for it, i.e. to swap or exchange it.

clue.text: Nuts beside small birds

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Nuts placed next to little birds, as on a bird table.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoos are a family of birds known for laying eggs in other species' nests.

clue.text: A virile gent turns, enthralling 50 grown-ups

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside the other
turns says the word for the virile man is read the other way round

parts.note: a stud is a sexually virile man
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A manly figure spins round, captivating fifty grown men and women.
explanation.walkthrough: STUD turned round is DUTS, and 'enthralling' puts L inside to give DULTS, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adults are fully grown people, the plain synonym of grown-ups.

clue.text: Cracked a nicer nut? Open to question

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so the letters of a nicer nut are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a broken nut nicer? It's debatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncertain is doubtful and not settled, so it remains open to question.

clue.text: Four seen entering sexual festival

indicators.note: seen entering says the numeral goes inside the other word

parts.note: carnal means relating to the body and sexual desire
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A foursome is spotted arriving at a raunchy party.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a public celebration with parades and revelry, a type of festival.

clue.text: Constable's work? Capture first of swindlers with cloak

parts.note: to land a fish or a contract is to capture it

indicators.note: first of picks out just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: A police constable's job: nabbing the leading swindler, who wears a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was the English painter of rural scenes such as The Hay Wain, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable is famous for paintings of countryside scenery, and the question mark flags his canvases as one example.

clue.text: Jumbo runs, consumed by mouse on ground

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten up, so the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed, so the letters of mouse on are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An elephant bolts, eaten up by a mouse running on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like an elephant's name but means huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo as an adjective means very large, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Going out to entertain Charlie is thrilling

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the word for going out holds the letter inside

parts.note: exiting means leaving or going out
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A night out spent hosting a friend called Charlie is great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting means causing eager enthusiasm, which is what thrilling describes.

clue.text: One contemplates husband eating trifle? On the contrary

indicators.note: eating suggests the husband would swallow the trifle
on the contrary reverses the eating, so the word for trifle swallows the husband's letter instead

parts.note: to tinker is to trifle or fiddle with something

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether the husband ate the dessert, then decides the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the dessert but is the verb tinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker is a person who contemplates or reflects deeply.

clue.text: Leader who died in ship's hold

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Admiral Lord ..., who died aboard HMS Victory at Trafalgar
second meaning: a wrestling hold applied from behind the opponent's neck

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone dying in a ship's cargo hold; split it after 'ship', with 's as link.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson, the British naval commander, was killed on his flagship; a full or half nelson is a wrestling grip.

clue.text: Former media, say

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: What the old media used to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link word for 'for example' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a view is to state or put it into words.

clue.text: Relishes people providing information on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: sources are informants who supply news

explanation.surface: Informants on air enjoy their work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic (British) accent the two words sound the same. 'Relishes' is a noun, condiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a tangy condiment, so sauces are relishes.

clue.text: Something that obstructs black bird, cutting head

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: cutting head means the first letter of the bird's name is removed

parts.note: a harrier is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark bird beheading something blocks the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is a fence, gate or other obstacle that prevents passage.

clue.text: Is in taxi turning over key

indicators.note: turning over says the combination is read backwards
in says the word is goes inside the word for taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A passenger turns over a key while sitting in a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like the thing being turned in the surface, but it is the definition, an adjective meaning essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental or essential, as does key in 'a key point'.

clue.text: Seems a paper's ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of a paper's are rearranged

explanation.surface: It looks as though a newspaper has been requested.
explanation.definitionFit: Appears is a verb meaning gives the impression of being, a synonym of seems.

clue.text: Following a newspaper lead in Essex, right?

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: lead in picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Checking whether a paper's top story covers Essex, the English county.
explanation.definitionFit: After as a preposition means later than or behind, the sense of following.

clue.text: Heroin — something fisherman might be on

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small sailing fishing boat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fisherman on drugs; 'on' means aboard instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is street slang for the opiate drug and also names a traditional single-masted fishing vessel.

clue.text: Hire actors, unfortunately ignoring current group of players

indicators.note: unfortunately signals that the letters of hire actors come out badly arranged
ignoring says one letter of the fodder is left out of the rearrangement

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Taking on actors was a mistake, especially overlooking the latest players.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of HIREACTORS and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is an ensemble of musicians performing together, so 'players' means instrumentalists.

clue.text: Scots rant about differences

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of scots rant are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scottish people complain loudly about disagreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrasts are striking dissimilarities between things, a synonym of differences.

clue.text: Stream bound to hold gallons

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the letter goes inside the word for certain

parts.note: bound as in certain, so it means sure

explanation.surface: A brook is certain to carry many gallons of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To surge is to rush forward in a powerful flow, as a crowd or water streams.
